title: Pulsefold: Contextual Lanes Rail + Compact Workspace Switcher Prototype
creator: Lena Park
description: Objective: Design and validate a compact, adaptive left-rail pattern (Pulsefold lanes) that surfaces per-workspace context (dashboards, rollouts, cost lenses) while enabling fast workspace switching and predictable routing. Scope: IA mapping, low/hi-fidelity prototypes, interaction spec for compact/expanded states, accessibility, and handoff artifacts for frontend and product. Goals: reduce second-to-click for common console tasks by 30%, provide a role-aware compact switcher for multi-tenant orgs, and create a deterministic routing model for deep links and rollouts. Constraints: must coexist with command palette, respect existing telemetry hooks, work within current layout grid, and be implementable without a console-wide redesign. Trade-offs discussed: single persistent rail vs. contextual transient lane (we recommend transient lanes appearing on hover/keyboard focus to save vertical space but keep a pin state for power users). Proposed pattern includes: 1) a top-level workspace chip with scoped quick-actions (dashboards, costs, rollouts), 2) lane microgrouping for per-route badges and SLO status, 3) compact workspace switcher that flips into full workspace directory with fuzzy search. Deliverables: Figma prototype, interaction spec, acceptance checklist, accessibility notes, and a rollout QA plan.
